newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FOCUS-KL blue-chip shares down at midday, off lows.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-KL blue-chip shares down at midday, off lows.

text.p: Malaysian shares continued to slide at midday on Tuesday after a sharp but brief recovery earlier in the day initiated by local institutions tentatively returning to the beleaguered market, dealers and analysts said.

At midday the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks stood at 888.25 points, down 13.89 points, or 1.54 percent. It reached a new 1997 low of 884.61 in morning trade.
The intraday rebound saw the index rising back above the 900-point mark momentarily, to 903.12.
Dealers and analysts said local institutions were back in the market looking for bargains.
"I can't imagine anyone else coming in. It could only be local (institutions)," said an analyst at a foreign brokerage in Kuala Lumpur.
"The market is fairly valued at these levels, so that would mean that we would not be rushing in," said the analyst.
Currency worries, however, continued to be the millstone around the market's neck. The ringgit hit a new 42-month low against the U.S. dollar earlier on Tuesday, falling to 2.7930.
"(Malaysian Prime Minister) Mahathir (Mohamad)'s statement on Friday caused concern for foreign investors," said a dealer at a local bank-backed brokerage.
Mahathir said on Friday he was "happy with the current level of the ringgit".
The sudden rebound in share prices in late morning was led by buying of Telekom Malaysia Bhd and Malayan Banking Bhd, rising 10 cents and 30 cents respectively, said the dealer.
Both stocks ended the morning session in negative territory.
The dealer said he had also seen some buying by Singapore-based institutions.
"There has been some nibbling from Singapore. They are fishing on the bottom," said the dealer.
But the buying soon ran out of steam.
"The rebound is purely technical, it looks like it's just going to be intraday. I don't know how long it is going to last," said a stock index futures trader at a local brokerage.
Newly-listed PPB Oil Palms Bhd reflected the market's overall bearishness. The stock debuted at 2.98 ringgit against a 2.80 ringgit offer price, but soon slipped back to 2.86 ringgit.
Calls by banks and brokerage houses on leveraged investors using shares as collateral to top up their portfolios with cash was also adding to the sell-down, said dealers.
